--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate PageRank scores for all nodes in the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate PageRank scores for all nodes in the graph. title: >- [Graph.pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Calculate PageRank scores for all nodes in the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate PageRank scores for all nodes in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L55481-L55682){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.pagerank( damping=0.85, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![PageRank](../assets/graphs/pagerank.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by PageRank. Hub C, linked from four neighbors, collects the most rank at 0.20, followed by E 0.17, D 0.16 and B 0.15, while the pendant node G gets the least." width="100%"} PageRank is a link analysis algorithm that assigns importance scores to nodes based on their incoming connections. Originally developed by Google to rank web pages, it's widely used in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and influence detection. The algorithm iteratively distributes "rank" from each node to its neighbors, with a damping factor to model random jumps. Nodes with many incoming edges from high-ranking nodes receive higher scores. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`), a node passes its rank along each outgoing edge in proportion to the edge's weight, so weights act as tie strengths, as in `networkx.pagerank()`. On an unweighted graph, or with `weighted=False`, every outgoing edge gets an equal share. In an undirected graph each edge can be followed both ways. Rank at a node with no outgoing edges is spread evenly over all nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [damping]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.85]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The probability of following an edge (vs. random jump). Higher values (closer to `1.0`) give more weight to the graph structure. Typical range: `0.8`-`0.95`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations to run. The algorithm stops early if convergence is reached. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. The algorithm stops when the sum of absolute differences between iterations is less than this value. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to split rank by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph: weights are used on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) and ignored otherwise. Pass `True` or `False` to override. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`; weights must be finite and non-negative. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store PageRank scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `pagerank`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to PageRank scores (sum to `1.0`). If `return_dict` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If weights are used and an edge has a negative, infinite or NaN weight. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~personalized_pagerank`) : PageRank with restarts at a chosen set of nodes. [](`~eigen_centrality`) : Importance from the importance of neighbors, without damping. [](`~katz_centrality`) : Like eigenvector centrality, with a baseline for every node. [](`~hub_centrality`), [](`~authority_centrality`) : The HITS scores, for directed graphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a small directed graph, PageRank favors nodes that are linked to by nodes that are themselves well linked. C is linked to by three nodes and ranks first, but D, linked to only by C, has nearly as much rank, and A, linked to only by D, nearly as much again. B and E, which nothing links to, get only the baseline share: ::: {#c7f78fc7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("E", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")], directed=True, ) graph.pagerank().get_node_df().sort("pagerank", descending=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

PageRank uses the weights, so frequent co-appearances count for more: ::: {#0d509d90 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} lesmis = ec.les_miserables().pagerank().cmty_louvain() ( lesmis.get_node_df() .select("label", "degree", "pagerank") .sort("pagerank", descending=True) .head(6) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Valjean is far ahead, with about twice the rank of Marius in second place. Drawing each character sized by rank and colored by community shows where that rank sits: ::: {#1e92bf7b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} lesmis.plot( color_by="cmty_louvain", size_by="pagerank", label_by="label", seed=3 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Rank isn't contact count Myriel, the bishop of the opening chapters, ranks third by PageRank but only eighteenth by degree: seven of the ten characters Myriel appears with appear with no one else, so the rank they get flows straight back to the bishop. Gavroche is the opposite case, second by degree but eighth by PageRank, meeting many characters but only a few times each. Here are the three characters' places by each measure: ::: {#f47c613b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl ( lesmis.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("pagerank", "degree").rank("min", descending=True) ) .filter(pl.col("label").is_in(["Valjean", "Myriel", "Gavroche"])) .sort("pagerank") .select("label", "pagerank", "degree") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Weighted versus unweighted Setting `weighted=False` counts every link the same, however many chapters it stands for. Gavroche rises from eighth to third and Javert from tenth to fifth, since both meet many characters a few times each, while Marius, whose ties are twice as heavy as the average, drops from second to fourth. The table gives the places both ways: ::: {#bbdf2573 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} lesmis.pagerank(weighted=False, attr_name="unweighted") ( lesmis.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("pagerank", "unweighted").rank("min", descending=True) ) .sort("unweighted") .select("label", "pagerank", "unweighted") .head(5) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Use the weighted ranks when the weights measure the strength of a tie, as here, and the unweighted ones when they measure something else, such as a distance or a cost. To rank characters by their closeness to a starting set (those nearest Cosette, say) rather than overall, use `personalized_pagerank()`. ### A citation network In a directed graph, rank flows along the edges. In the `citations()` network it flows from each paper to the papers it cites, so the seminal Moreau 2000 ranks first and Nakamura 2001, the first of the learning papers, second. HITS, which follows the survey's references, puts Nakamura only eighteenth by `authority_centrality()`: ::: {#ba2bd01a .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} citations = ec.citations().pagerank() citations.plot(layout="pos", color_by="pagerank", label_by="label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
